crops.prompt: Create ONE landscape 3:2 documentary garden photograph for the Carrot growing-guide header in a British gardening book. This must show living carrots GROWING IN SOIL, as an ordinary attentive gardener would photograph them, not harvested produce, not a cutout or arranged still life. Use reference 1, John's real home-garden bed, for the ground texture, muted practical paving and plausible setting; frame much closer and down into the bed so no new architecture is needed. Use reference 2 only for real carrot foliage and crown anatomy. Camera at a low crouching height and tilted down slightly, natural 50mm-like perspective, looking along a short planted row. A near clump of finely divided feathery carrot tops grows from several closely spaced crowns near the centre-right; two different orange shoulders just peek 1–2 cm above slightly settled crumbly dark soil, with all of the long roots remaining underground. Smaller plants and natural gaps recede to the left and into the back, varied lean and maturity, untidy interweaving foliage rather than regular identical bouquets. The orange shoulders must be subtle and believable, never long roots exposed upright above the soil. Include visible ordinary damp brown earth with a few small stones, fibrous compost and one tiny weed, not a perfect compost texture. A subdued sliver of the pale worn garden edging may appear at the far upper-left, no invented path across the bed. Soft bright overcast Cornish daylight, natural restrained greens and orange, readable middle tones, gentle shadows, modest depth of field but enough detail in soil and neighbouring foliage to feel like a real handheld garden photograph. Balanced crop composition with main plant on the right half and a little open ground on the left; safe to crop square or as a horizontal 2:1 header. No people, tools, signs, text, borders, labels, artificial lighting, lens flare, decorative props or supermarket perfection. Generate a NEW photograph inspired by the references; do not reproduce any existing page.
crops.assumption: A close view into the home-garden bed at mature summer growth; reconstructed planting, not a documentary record of a dated crop.

crops.prompt: Create ONE landscape 3:2 documentary garden photograph for the Kale growing-guide header in a British gardening book. Living kale plants GROWING IN SOIL in a real Cornish allotment, an ordinary handheld photograph by the gardener; not harvested leaves, a cutout, studio arrangement or staged perfection. Reference 1 is John's actual camera photograph: use its ground-level garden feel, crumbly soil, worn narrow brick path at the right and natural daylight as the setting authority. Reference 2 is an approved winter kale reconstruction in the same bed: use it only to establish believable Cavolo Nero plant structure and the local layout, and take a much closer new view. Crouch beside the path and photograph one healthy but irregular Cavolo Nero plant on the right half of the image, from a modest downward three-quarter angle. Its lower stem clearly enters dark soil, with a few real picked-leaf scars, one modest ageing outer leaf, long narrow slate-green puckered leaves arching at different angles and young shorter upright leaves. Neighbouring smaller plants recede into the left/back with partially hidden silhouettes, no repeated symmetrical palm-like fans and no giant geometric bubble texture. Show enough soil and a small worn flush path edge to make the growing situation immediately clear. The near leaf surface is detailed, the background bed gently softer, no exaggerated bokeh or invented structures. Soft bright overcast autumn daylight, natural blue-green foliage and brown earth, usable print midtones without muddy blacks. Main crown and stem fit in the frame, important plant detail in central-right safe area so square or 2:1 horizontal header crops work. Frame tight enough that distant houses and skyline are outside the photograph. Natural plant-to-plant variation, slight leaf overlap and ordinary uneven soil. No people, tools, labels, text, borders, dramatic lighting or decorative props. Generate a new garden photograph grounded in these references.
crops.assumption: Autumn Cavolo Nero in the allotment bed; close planting reconstruction based on the real soil/path view and approved winter plant study.
